The nearly $1 billion plant will process "black mass"—a powder containing metals like lithium, cobalt, and nickel from used batteries—into essential cathode-grade materials. Prediction target period: from 2024-02-14 to 2024-02-29. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> A briefing published by the Natural Resource Governance Institute on December 20, 2023, analyzed a U.S.-supported initiative for the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Zambia to establish a joint manufacturing plant for nickel, manganese, and cobalt (NMC) battery precursors. [6] The report confirmed that planning for the plant was actively underway in 2023, part of a broader effort to build a regional value chain for electric vehicle (EV) batteries and add value to locally extracted minerals. [6] However, the briefing highlighted that there was limited public information on the specific support the U.S. and EU intend to provide to the project. [6] The U.S. had previously signed a memorandum of understanding with the DRC and Zambia in December 2022 to support the development of this EV battery supply chain. [2, 3, 4] <2> On October 30, 2023, global commodities giant Glencore released its production results for the third quarter of 2023, covering the nine months ending September 30, 2023. The report indicated that the company's own-sourced cobalt production totaled 32,500 tonnes year-to-date, a 2% decrease from the 33,100 tonnes produced in the same period of 2022. Despite this slight decline, Glencore maintained its full-year production guidance for cobalt, adjusting the range to 38 ± 4 kilotonnes from a previous 38 ± 5 kilotonnes. <3> In late October 2023, an article from MetalMiner reported a "perfect storm" for cobalt prices, causing the metal's price index to hit a record low. The price crash was attributed to a combination of a global oversupply and a simultaneous slowdown in demand from the battery market. The report specifically cited declining electric vehicle sales in Europe and China as a major contributing factor to this market downturn. <4> A seven-party Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed to develop the Lobito Corridor, a project aimed at creating a new export route for critical minerals from Central Africa to the Atlantic Ocean. The signatories include the United States, the European Union, Angola, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Zambia, the African Development Bank, and the Africa Finance Corporation. [4, 6] This strategic infrastructure initiative is designed to enhance regional trade, support supply chain diversification, and connect the mineral-rich regions of the DRC and Zambia to the Port of Lobito in Angola. [6, 7] The agreement outlines a collaborative effort across multiple sectors to unlock the economic potential of the corridor, which includes the development of the new Zambia-Lobito rail line. [4, 6] The Africa Finance Corporation has been appointed as the lead project developer to oversee the necessary feasibility and preparatory studies. [5] <5> Li-Cycle announced on October 23, 2023, that it was pausing construction of its Rochester, New York, hub due to escalating costs. The facility, located at Eastman Business Park, was poised to become a major player in the North American battery recycling landscape, bolstering the domestic circular economy for battery metals by processing battery materials into critical, battery-grade lithium, nickel, and cobalt. Although construction is paused, the project's engineering and procurement phases are largely complete. <6> Vale, a significant cobalt supplier, announced in its Q3 2023 production report on October 17, 2023, that its nickel production for the quarter ending September 30, 2023, saw a 19% decrease year-over-year. [1, 2, 3] Cobalt is produced as a byproduct of this nickel extraction. The company stated the decline was planned and primarily attributed it to the ongoing transition to underground mining operations at its Voisey's Bay mine in Canada, along with additional maintenance at the Sudbury refinery. [1, 2, 3] <7> A report by S&P Global, published on October 5, 2023, confirmed that cobalt prices weakened during September 2023 as a result of slow demand. [2] The report highlighted a lack of restocking ahead of China's National Day holiday, which ran from September 29th to October 6th, indicating a delay in seasonal peak demand and consequently putting pressure on prices. [2] The Platts-assessed cobalt 99.8% European price decreased by $0.88/lb between September 1st and 14th, before a slight recovery. [2] This trend of weak demand was also observed in the lithium market. [10] <8> Madagascar-based nickel and cobalt producer Ambatovy reported a disruption and slurry leak on its 220-kilometer pipeline on September 25, 2023. [5, 10] The incident, which occurred around 5:30 AM local time near the fokontany of Ankorabe, prompted an immediate halt to pipeline operations. [10] The pipeline is crucial for transporting ore from the mine site near Moramanga to the processing and refinery plant in Toamasina. [10] Ambatovy, majority-owned by Japan's Sumitomo Corporation, dispatched technical teams to assess the cause and extent of the damage, with no injuries reported. [5, 7] While the company evaluated the timeline for recovery, traders expressed concern that a shutdown lasting more than two months could tighten supplies in the cobalt market. [3, 4, 9] The company notified relevant authorities and began distributing potable water to surrounding communities. [5, 10] <9> A September 2023 market report highlighted the continued weakness in the global cobalt market, characterized by significant oversupply, low demand, and falling prices. The combination of these factors was evident in the price for standard grade cobalt, which stood at $13.50-$14.75 per pound on September 14, a substantial decrease from the $16.30-$18.50 per pound seen in mid-July. Traders reported slower-than-usual buying activity for September, and analysts forecast considerable market surpluses of 7,000 tonnes for 2023 and 14,000 tonnes for 2024. A key contributing factor to the weak demand was the ongoing shift in the electric vehicle battery market away from nickel-cobalt-manganese (NCM) chemistry and towards cobalt-free lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) batteries.

The new Naxtra batteries are said to have an energy density of 175 Wh/kg, comparable to some Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) batteries, and can offer a range of up to 500 kilometers. The award recognizes ABTC's innovative, internally-developed de-manufacturing and selective hydrometallurgical recycling process. This two-phase system stands apart from traditional smelting and shredding by enabling high recovery rates of critical materials such as lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese, copper, and aluminum. A key feature of the technology is its feedstock-agnostic capability, allowing it to process various sizes and chemistries of lithium-ion batteries while promoting sustainability through reduced waste and pollution. <3> On March 20, 2025, President Donald J. Trump signed the Executive Order titled 'Immediate Measures to Increase American Mineral Production' to bolster national security by reducing reliance on foreign mineral sources. [1, 3, 5] The order aims to fast-track the permitting and development of domestic mining projects for a range of materials defined as 'minerals', which includes not only the official list of critical minerals but also specifies uranium, copper, potash, and gold. [2, 4, 10] It mandates federal agencies to identify priority projects for which permits can be expedited or immediately issued and to compile a list of all federal lands with known mineral deposits within 10 days. [4, 7, 9] The order also directs the use of the Defense Production Act and mobilizes various financial tools, including the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation, to provide capital and support for new domestic mineral production projects. [5, 6, 8] <4> In response to market imbalances, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) imposed an export ban on cobalt concentrate, which took effect on February 22, 2025. [2] [1, 4] The action had a significant impact on the global supply chain, given the DRC's control of 70% of the world's cobalt, with some estimates suggesting the removal of over 100,000 tonnes from the market over a seven-month period. [5, 6] Consequently, cobalt prices surged. [3, 5, 7, 8] [3] In Europe, prices climbed from $9.95 per pound on February 24 to $12.25 by March 7. [8] <5> An analysis of the electric vehicle (EV) market in 2025 indicates the average cost of battery packs has fallen to approximately $130 per kWh. [1] This represents a significant price reduction over the last 15 years, with costs dropping from over $1,100 per kWh in 2010, $350 per kWh in 2015, and $200 per kWh in 2020. [2, 6] Announced on February 22, 2025, the new measures included a temporary four-month ban on all cobalt exports, granting the state-owned Entreprise Generale du Cobalt (EGC) exclusive rights to export hand-dug cobalt, and strictly separating artisanal and industrial cobalt production. [1, 4] These regulations effectively removed a significant amount of supply from informal channels. <7> In early 2025, cobalt prices experienced a significant surge, with standard-grade metal reaching as high as $15.75 per pound.
